      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "note": "I-A exact sequence is a standard special Hopf reference. Target supplies general circle-bundle degree-k argument locally; do not substitute special-k statement as proof of all-k classification.",

      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"

        "line_start": 2321,
        "line_end": 2328
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "case interpreted as \\(\\mathbb Z\\).  Since \\(P\\simeq S^3\\) is simply\nconnected, \\(|k|=1\\).  The two signs are exchanged by reversing either the fibre orientation or\nthe base orientation, with the other held fixed; simultaneous reversal of\nboth preserves \\(k\\).  Indeed,\n\\(k=\\langle c_1(P),[S^2]\\rangle\\), and these two reversals negate\n\\(c_1(P)\\) and \\([S^2]\\), respectively.  With the Paper-I-A oriented\nrepresentative, \\(k=+1\\).\n\\end{proof}",

      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0018",

      "source_use_excerpt": "The oriented principal-bundle result\n\\(c_1(P)=+1\\) fixes the primitive Hopf bundle, not a physical associated\ncharacter sector.         "line_start": 2343,
        "line_end": 2367
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Fix the chosen left-fiber Paper-I-A representative of this conjugacy class.\nLet\n\\[\n\\eta_0:=\\eta/\\Rmom\n\\]\nbe its dimensionless principal \\(U(1)\\)-connection.  The bundle is\n\\[\n\\Sone\\hookrightarrow S^3(\\Rmom)\\longrightarrow S^2.\n\\]\nThen\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{p2:eq:eta0}\n\\oint_{S^1}\\eta_0=2\\pi,\n\\qquad\n d\\eta_0=\\pi^*\\omega,\n\\qquad\n\\frac{1}{2\\pi}\\int_{S^2}\\omega = 1,\n\\end{equation}\nso \\(c_1(P)=1\\).  We use \\(\\eta_0\\) as a representative of the\nhomogeneous Reeb-normalized principal-connection gauge class.  Gauge-related\nprincipal forms are the same unmarked connection realization; the displayed\nrepresentative is not an additional physical selector.  Every invariant\nconclusion below is unchanged under conjugating the maximal torus; axis- or\nhandedness-dependent formulas are convention-relative.\n",

        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2435,
        "line_end": 2458
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nFor a homogeneous scalar multiple \\(s\\eta_0\\), the principal vertical\nnormalization is\n\\((s\\eta_0)(\\xi_0)=s\\), so it forces \\(s=1\\).  This uniqueness statement is\nonly within the homogeneous scalar-multiple family; it does not exclude\ndistinct gauge-related principal connections such as\n\\(\\eta_0-\\pi^*d\\bar\\chi\\) for a smooth real function\n\\(\\bar\\chi\\) on \\(S^2\\) with \\(d\\bar\\chi\\not\\equiv0\\).\nUsing \\eqref{p2:eq:eta0} and fiber integration directly in the main proof gives\n\\[\n \\int_{S^3}\\eta_0\\wedge d\\eta_0\n =\\int_{S^2}\\!\\left(\\oint_{S^1}\\eta_0\\right)\\omega\n =(2\\pi)(2\\pi)=4\\pi^2,\n\\]\nand hence \\(Q_{\\CS}[\\eta_0]=1\\) in the convention\n\\eqref{p2:eq:cs}.  Applying the character differential\n\\(d\\rho_q:q\\) to the principal connection and curvature gives\n\\(A_q=q\\eta_0-d\\chi\\) and \\(F_q=q\\omega\\); hence\n\\(c_1(L^q)=q[\\omega/(2\\pi)]=q\\).  For\n\\(A_s=s\\eta_0-d\\chi\\), the exact gauge term integrates to zero on closed\n\\(S^3\\), so quadratic scaling gives\n\\(Q_{\\CS}[A_s]=s^2\\).  Applying this with \\(s=q\\) proves the associated-line\nclaim.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0022",

    {
      "from": "p1:prop:contact-normalization",
      "to": "BH-IID-U-prequantum-symplectic-normalization",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "BASE_AREA_CURVATURE_NORMALIZATION",
      "scope_guard": "BASE_AREA_CURVATURE_NORMALIZATION",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2517,
        "line_end": 2522
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "We use the Hopf/contact normalization established in Paper~I-A \\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Thus the Hopf fibration \\(\\Sone \\hookrightarrow S^3 \\xrightarrow{\\pi} S^2\\) realizes $S^3(\\Rmom)$ as a principal $\\mathrm{U}(1)$-bundle over the symplectic manifold $(S^2(\\Rmom/2),\\omega)$. Let $\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}$ denote the Riemannian area form, so $\\int_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}=\\pi \\Rmom^2$. We take the normalized symplectic form\n\\[\n\\omega := \\frac{2}{\\Rmom^2}\\,\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)},\\qquad \\int_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}\\omega = 2\\pi,\n\\]\nso that the associated complex line bundle $L\\to S^2(\\Rmom/2)$ has $c_1(L)=[\\omega]/(2\\pi)=1$.\n",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0030",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-BH-IID-U-prequantum-symplectic-normalization",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {

        "line_end": 2544
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nPaper~I-A proves this degree-one Boothby--Wang normalization\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  The displayed equations translate its physical and\ndimensionless connections into Paper-II notation.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0031",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:prop:hopf-connection-prequantum-bundle",

    {
      "from": "p1:prop:hopf-scale-dictionary",
      "to": "p2:prop:hopf-connection-prequantum-bundle",

        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2526,
        "line_end": 2537
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Let $\\eta_0$ denote the \\emph{dimensionless} principal $\\mathrm{U}(1)$-connection 1-form on the Hopf bundle $S^3\\to S^2$, with principal generator $\\xi_0$ normalized by $\\eta_0(\\xi_0)=1$, and set\n\\[\n\\eta := \\Rmom\\,\\eta_0,\n\\qquad\n\\xi:=\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0.\n\\]\nThe metric-scaled contact form is normalized by $\\eta(\\xi)=1$.\nThen the curvature of the principal connection is \\cite{blair2010contact,boyer2008sasakian}\n\\[\nd\\eta_0 = \\pi^* \\omega,\n\\]\nso \\((S^3, \\eta_0)\\) is a prequantum circle bundle over \\((S^2, \\omega)\\) with integer Chern class \\(c_1 = 1\\).",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0032",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:prop:hopf-connection-prequantum-bundle",

    },

      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThe first two identities are the declared principal-to-metric transport.\nSubstitution gives\n\\(\\eta(\\xi)=(\\Rmom\\eta_0)(\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0)=1\\), and constancy of\n\\(\\Rmom\\) on the round host gives\n\\(d\\eta=\\Rmom\\,d\\eta_0=\\Rmom\\,\\pi^*\\omega\\).\nOmitting any declared output gives a closure defect once the dictionary is\nlicensed; multiplying either output by an additional free scalar changes the\ngenerated normalization relation.  The remaining quantities occupy distinct\nowner or associated-line slots and therefore are not fixed by this graph.\n\\end{proof}\n",

        "line_start": 2606,
        "line_end": 2623
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Let $\\psi\\sim\\psi+4\\pi$ be the standard Hopf fiber angle on\n$S^3\\cong SU(2)$, so that the chosen left-fiber Hopf action is\n\\[\n g\\longmapsto h_\\theta g,\n \\qquad\n h_\\theta:=\\exp(i\\theta\\sigma_3/2),\n \\qquad \\theta\\sim\\theta+4\\pi.\n\\]\nThe Reeb vector field $\\xi = \\frac{2}{\\Rmom}\\partial_\\psi$ generates this fiber action on $S^3(\\Rmom)$. A field $\\phi \\in C^\\infty(S^3)$ has \\textbf{integer Hopf charge} $q \\in \\ZZ$ if\n\\begin{equation}\n\\partial_\\psi \\phi = i\\frac{q}{2}\\,\\phi,\n\\qquad\n\\xi(\\phi)=\\frac{i q}{\\Rmom}\\,\\phi,\n\\qquad\n\\phi(h_\\theta g)=e^{i(q/2)\\theta}\\phi(g).\n\\label{p2:eq:hopf-charge-convention}\n\\end{equation}\nEquivalently, if one uses the $2\\pi$-periodic principal-$U(1)$ parameter $\\alpha=\\theta/2$, the character is $e^{iq\\alpha}$.  The Hilbert space decomposes as $L^2(S^3) = \\bigoplus_{q \\in \\ZZ} \\mathcal{V}_q$, where $\\mathcal{V}_q$ consists of charge-$q$ fields.",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0034",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:def:hopf-charge",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_start": 2627,
        "line_end": 2636
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Charge-$q$ fields are sections of the line bundle $L^q \\to S^2$, where\n$L$ is the degree-one bundle associated to the chosen left-fiber Hopf\nrepresentative. The case $q = 0$ corresponds to functions on the base $S^2$\npulled back to $S^3$; $q \\neq 0$ corresponds to genuinely ``twisted'' fields\nthat cannot be defined on $S^2$ alone.  Throughout this section, $q$ denotes\nthe integer geometric Hopf charge and $q/2$ is the exponent of its\nleft-fiber character in the \\(4\\pi\\) parameter.  This exponent is not\nidentified with the projected Berry label \\(r\\), and both are distinct from\nthe finite diagonal spin weight $\\mathfrak s$ used in the preceding\nfinite-module projector notation.",

      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-UNLABELED:Paper2D:remark:2625",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

    {
      "from": "p1:thm:lichnerowicz-s3",
      "to": "p2:thm:lichnerowicz",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "ROUND_UNTWISTED_LICHNEROWICZ",

      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2787,
        "line_end": 2791
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThis is the round-\\(S^3\\) Lichnerowicz identity recorded in\nPaper~I-A~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  It is repeated here only to state the\nkinematic no-zero consequence.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0044",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:thm:lichnerowicz",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {
      "from": "p2:thm:lichnerowicz",
      "to": "p2:cor:fermion-gap",
      "kind": "PREMISE_OF",
      "branch_id": "LICHNEROWICZ_ESTIMATE",
      "scope_guard": "LICHNEROWICZ_ESTIMATE",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2802,
        "line_end": 2806
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nFrom Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:lichnerowicz}, $D_{S^3}^{\\,2}=\\nabla^*\\nabla+\\frac{3}{2\\Rmom^2}$.\nSince $\\nabla^*\\nabla$ is non-negative, every Dirac eigenvalue $\\lambda$ satisfies the displayed bound.\n\\end{proof}\n",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0045",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:cor:fermion-gap",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {
      "from": "p2:thm:dirac-spectrum",
      "to": "p2:cor:fermion-gap",
      "kind": "CITATION_ONLY",
      "branch_id": "EXACT_GAP_FORWARD_COMPARISON",
      "scope_guard": "EXACT_GAP_FORWARD_COMPARISON",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2798,
        "line_end": 2799
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\]\nIn particular, the Lichnerowicz identity rules out harmonic spinors on the positively curved round $S^3$. The sharper exact gap is obtained from the round-sphere spectrum in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}.",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "note": "The Lichnerowicz bound does not require the later exact spectrum; source points forward only for sharper gap.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0046",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:cor:fermion-gap",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {
      "from": "p1:thm:representation-harmonic-package",
      "to": "p2:thm:dirac-spectrum",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "ROUND_SPIN_DIRAC_SPECTRUM",
      "scope_guard": "ROUND_SPIN_DIRAC_SPECTRUM",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2824,
        "line_end": 2829
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThe eigenvalues, per-sign multiplicities, and exact first gap are the spinor\npart of the Paper-I-A round-\\(S^3\\) harmonic package\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Paper~II imports this only as a kinematic continuum\nspectrum.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "note": "Spinor part only; scalar/Casimir finite package is not substituted for untwisted Dirac spectrum.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0047",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:thm:dirac-spectrum",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {
      "from": "p2:thm:dirac-spectrum",
      "to": "p2:cor:no-dirac-zero",
      "kind": "PREMISE_OF",
      "branch_id": "NO_ZERO_EXACT_GAP",
      "scope_guard": "NO_ZERO_EXACT_GAP",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2843,
        "line_end": 2845
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThe Dirac spectrum in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum} is $\\pm(k+3/2)/\\Rmom$ with $k\\ge 0$, so $0$ is not an eigenvalue and the smallest absolute eigenvalue is $3/(2\\Rmom)$.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0048",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:cor:no-dirac-zero",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {
      "from": "p2:thm:lichnerowicz",
      "to": "UNLABELED:Paper2D:remark:2847",
      "kind": "PREMISE_OF",
      "branch_id": "ROUND_BOUND_VS_EXACT",
      "scope_guard": "ROUND_BOUND_VS_EXACT",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2849,
        "line_end": 2861
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "On a closed Riemannian spin manifold \\((M,g)\\), the Lichnerowicz identity\nimplies for every Dirac eigenvalue \\(\\lambda\\) that\n\\[\n\\lambda^2\\ge\\frac14\\min_M\\scal_g.\n\\]\nFor the round \\(S^3(\\Rmom)\\), one has\n\\(\\scal_g=6/\\Rmom^2\\), so\n\\[\n|\\lambda|\\ge\\frac{\\sqrt{3/2}}{\\Rmom}.\n\\]\nThis lower bound proves positivity and excludes zero modes, but it is weaker\nthan the exact first absolute eigenvalue \\(3/(2\\Rmom)\\), which comes from\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}, not from the Lichnerowicz estimate alone.",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0049",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-UNLABELED:Paper2D:remark:2847",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {
      "from": "p2:thm:dirac-spectrum",
      "to": "UNLABELED:Paper2D:remark:2847",
      "kind": "PREMISE_OF",
      "branch_id": "ROUND_BOUND_VS_EXACT",
      "scope_guard": "ROUND_BOUND_VS_EXACT",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",

        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2858,

      "source_use_excerpt": "\\]\nThis lower bound proves positivity and excludes zero modes, but it is weaker\nthan the exact first absolute eigenvalue \\(3/(2\\Rmom)\\), which comes from\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}, not from the Lichnerowicz estimate alone.",

        "file": "Paper2F-TechnicalMaterial-v1_60.tex",
        "line_start": 7265,
        "line_end": 7272
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "The diagonal-weight table above gives\n\\[\n\\dim_\\CC \\mathcal H_1^{(-1/2)}=\\dim_\\CC \\mathcal H_1^{(+1/2)}=2.\n\\]\nThe preceding proposition shows that the Fourier-averaging projectors onto \\(\\mathfrak s=\\pm\\tfrac12\\) isolate exactly those two sectors. Their direct sum is therefore the protected carrier.  Although the projector formula uses a chosen Cartan axis, the resulting direct sum is the invariant spinor submodule \\(V_{1/2,0}\\oplus V_{0,1/2}\\) inside \\(\\mathcal H_1\\).\n\\end{proof}\n\nThe diagonal-weight grading therefore isolates the protected eight-real-dimensional spinor module as a canonical-relative kinematic block. Later operator or coupling bases may realize this block, but any physical low-energy identification requires finite-field and dynamical closure in later papers.",

      "scope_guard": "EXACT_LEVEL1_WEIGHT_TABLE_ONLY",

      "branch_id": "ONLY_IMPORTED_SOURCE_CLAUSE",

    {
      "from": "p1:thm:hodge-one-form-spectrum",
      "to": "p2:thm:spin1-spectrum",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "COEXACT_ONE_FORMS",
      "scope_guard": "COEXACT_ONE_FORMS",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2930,
        "line_end": 2946
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nOn $S^3$, the Hodge decomposition for $1$-forms is $\\Omega^1 = d\\Omega^0 \\oplus d^\\dagger\\Omega^2$ since the space of harmonic $1$-forms vanishes ($H^1(S^3)=0$). \n\n\\textbf{Exact branch.}\nLet $f$ be a scalar eigenfunction with $\\Delta_{S^3} f = \\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2} f$ and $k\\ge 1$. Then\n\\[\n\\Delta_1(df)=d(\\Delta_{S^3} f)=\\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2}\\,df,\n\\]\nso $df$ is an eigen-$1$-form with the same eigenvalue. The scalar eigenspace has dimension $(k+1)^2$. For $k\\ge1$, no nonzero scalar eigenfunction is constant, so $d:E_k\\to\\Omega^1(S^3)$ is injective and $\\dim(dE_k)=(k+1)^2$. Constants occur only in the $k=0$ scalar eigenspace and do not enter the exact branch listed here.\n\n\\textbf{Coexact branch.}\nFor a coexact $1$-form $\\varpi$ with $d^\\dagger\\varpi=0$, in dimension $3$ the coexact branch is conventionally described by the curl operator.  With the self-adjoint curl convention\n\\[\nC:=\\star d\\quad\\text{on coexact one-forms},\n\\]\nup to the harmless sign fixed by the Hodge-star convention one has \\(\\Delta_1\\varpi=C^2\\varpi\\).  The curl spectrum on $S^3(\\Rmom)$ is $\\mathrm{Spec}(C)=\\{\\pm\\frac{k+1}{\\Rmom}:k\\ge 1\\}$, hence the coexact eigenvalues are $\\frac{(k+1)^2}{\\Rmom^2}$. The stated multiplicities are the standard vector-harmonic multiplicities. \\cite{Camporesi1991,besse1978manifolds}\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Source-use/type mapping only; E1/E3/E4 reviewers own correctness adjudication.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B4-EDGE-0001",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B4-ROUTE-p2:thm:spin1-spectrum",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {
      "from": "p2:cor:laplace-spectrum",
      "to": "p2:thm:spin1-spectrum",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "EXACT_ONE_FORMS",
      "scope_guard": "EXACT_ONE_FORMS",
      "logic_group": "AND",
      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2933,
        "line_end": 2939
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\textbf{Exact branch.}\nLet $f$ be a scalar eigenfunction with $\\Delta_{S^3} f = \\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2} f$ and $k\\ge 1$. Then\n\\[\n\\Delta_1(df)=d(\\Delta_{S^3} f)=\\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2}\\,df,\n\\]\nso $df$ is an eigen-$1$-form with the same eigenvalue. The scalar eigenspace has dimension $(k+1)^2$. For $k\\ge1$, no nonzero scalar eigenfunction is constant, so $d:E_k\\to\\Omega^1(S^3)$ is injective and $\\dim(dE_k)=(k+1)^2$. Constants occur only in the $k=0$ scalar eigenspace and do not enter the exact branch listed here.\n",

      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nAt the cutoff $\\Lambda_L$, the scalar level $L$ is included because $L(L+2)/\\Rmom^2<\\Lambda_L$, while level $L+1$ is excluded since $(L+1)(L+3)/\\Rmom^2>\\Lambda_L$.         "line_end": 3326
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "On the fixed full momentum carrier \\(\\mathcal H_p=\\mathcal H_1\\),\nuse the primitive left generator \\(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\\).\nThen\n\\[\n \\mathcal H_1|_{U(1)_H}\n =7\\chi_0\\oplus3\\chi_1\\oplus3\\chi_{-1}\\oplus\\chi_2\\oplus\\chi_{-2},\n \\qquad Q_H(Q_H^2-I)(Q_H^2-4I)=0.\n\\]\nIts multiplicities at \\(q=-2,-1,0,1,2\\) are \\(1,3,7,3,1\\).\nIn this left convention the extreme weights \\(q=\\pm2\\) occur in\n\\(V_{0,1}\\); for the geometric right convention they occur in \\(V_{1,0}\\).\nThey are absent from the scalar harmonic submodule \\(E_0\\oplus E_1\\).\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nOn \\(V_{j_L,j_R}\\), the charge is \\(-2m_R\\) with multiplicity \\(2j_L+1\\).\nThe six summands contribute, in the order\n\\((0,0),(\\tfrac12,0),(0,\\tfrac12),\n(\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12),(1,0),(0,1)\\),\n\\[\n \\chi_0,\\quad 2\\chi_0,\\quad\n \\chi_{-1}+\\chi_1,\\quad 2\\chi_{-1}+2\\chi_1,\\quad\n 3\\chi_0,\\quad \\chi_{-2}+\\chi_0+\\chi_2.\n\\]\nSumming gives the stated character and hence the polynomial identity.",

        "line_start": 3373,
        "line_end": 3392
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "For\n$\\mathcal P_x(m_x)=\\bigoplus_{k=0}^{m_x}E_k^x$ with\n$E_k^x\\cong V_{k/2}\\otimes V_{k/2}^*$, degree $k$ has weights\n$-k,-k+2,\\ldots,k$, each with multiplicity $k+1$.  Hence\n\\[\n \\operatorname{spec}(Q_H|_{\\mathcal P_x(m_x)})=\\{-m_x,\\ldots,m_x\\}.\n\\]\nFor $|q|\\le m_x$, writing\n$r=\\lfloor(m_x-|q|)/2\\rfloor$, the exact multiplicity is\n\\[\n d_{m_x}(q)=(r+1)(|q|+1+r),\n\\]\nand\n\\[\n D_{m_x}:=\\dim\\mathcal P_x(m_x)\n =\\frac{(m_x+1)(m_x+2)(2m_x+3)}6.\n\\]\nThus $m_p=1$ does not impose a universal bound on later position-clock\nweights.\n\\end{proposition}",
      "verification_limit": "Source-use/type mapping only; E1/E3/E4 reviewers own correctness adjudication.",

      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",

        "line_start": 3402,
        "line_end": 3432
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Use the left-action convention of\nCorollary~\\ref{p2d:cor:hopf-rotation-transvection}, and set\n\\[\n Q_i:=Q_{H,L,i}^{x}=-2L_{i,x}^-.\n\\]\nFor the nonnegative scalar Laplacian restricted to this band,\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\sum_{i=1}^{3}Q_i^2=a^2\\Delta_a.}\n\\]\nFor every spectral weight \\(W=w(\\Delta_a)\\) on the band,\n\\[\n \\operatorname{Tr}(WQ_iQ_j)\n =\\frac{a^2\\delta_{ij}}{3}\\operatorname{Tr}(W\\Delta_a).\n\\]\nThe same identities hold for the explicitly chosen right chiral triple\n\\(Q_i=2L_{i,x}^+\\).  They concern complete scalar bands and chiral\ngenerators; no clock-energy calibration or Hamiltonian premise is used.\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nOn \\(E_k^x\\), the chosen chiral factor has spin \\(j=k/2\\), so\n\\[\n \\sum_iQ_i^2=4j(j+1)I=k(k+2)I=a^2\\Delta_a|_{E_k^x}.\n\\]\nThe complete band is invariant under the chiral action, so the finite direct\nsum proves the operator identity without a compression defect.\nThe weight \\(W\\) commutes with that action; hence\n\\(T_{ij}:=\\operatorname{Tr}(WQ_iQ_j)\\) is an invariant two-tensor for\nthe adjoint \\(SO(3)\\) action and equals \\(c\\delta_{ij}\\).\nSumming its diagonal entries gives\n\\(3c=a^2\\operatorname{Tr}(W\\Delta_a)\\).",
      "verification_limit": "Source-use/type mapping only; E1/E3/E4 reviewers own correctness adjudication.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B4-EDGE-0027",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B4-ROUTE-p2d:cor:chiral-scalar-casimir-identity",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_end": 3500

      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nCorollary~\\ref{p2d:cor:hopf-rotation-transvection} identifies the\nleft-action operator with $-i\\mathcal V_i^L$; rescaling radius gives\n$D_i=(\\hbar/a)Q_i$. A Killing field commutes with the round scalar\nLaplacian, hence $D_i$ preserves each $E_k^x$, establishing the exact\nrestriction and its chiral Casimir square. Restricting the\nfinite square to $E_k^x$ yields\n$\\hbar^2k(k+2)/a^2$.\nThe finite-rank extension has a smooth kernel (the finite band is a sum\nof smooth eigenspaces), and is therefore smoothing.       "source_use_excerpt": "\\end{proof}\nThese are the native fixed-observable hypotheses required before using\noperator-system spectral recovery technology\n\\cite{LitGEOVanSuijlekom2020Truncation}.  The theorem proves the expectation\ncertificate; it does not assert a full quantum-metric convergence theorem\nwithout its own uniform metric estimates.  For compressed comparisons,\nTheorem~\\ref{p2b:thm:v2210-lit-word-defect} computes the first error.\nActual source derivatives and moving comparison maps are included in the\ndifferentiated word; an undifferentiated expectation bound is not a jet bound.\n\nFor the native two-dimensional center, the explicit sector-tagged comparison\nof Paper~II-C,\nCorollary~\\ref{p2c:cor:v2211-tagged-intrinsic-populations}, evaluates both\nerrors in this theorem to zero for every central word.  Its maps are a\nmultiplicative classical tag embedding and an explicit unital completely\npositive retraction.  This supplies a completed finite comparison on that\nclaim algebra.  It does not extend the certificate to noncentral source\nwords, repair the quaternion rule's quadratic aliasing, or provide an\ninjective all-resolution map into the frozen momentum carrier.",

# Independent verification certificates — Paper II-D batch 1

Input: `Sources-v2_366/Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex`, lines 1–1016,
source corpus v2.366. Reviewer: `/root/independent_checks`.
No inherited audit verdict or other agent's proposal was consulted before these
provisional certificates. These arguments verify existing propositions only.
They do not establish occurrence, a Hamiltonian, a dispersion identification,
or global physical realization.

<a id="HEAT-001"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-HEAT-001 — finite semigroup

A commuting family of finite-dimensional self-adjoint operators is
simultaneously diagonalizable. The semigroup law makes the family commute.
In a joint eigenline its eigenvalue is a continuous multiplicative function
v(t) in [0,1] with v(0)=1. It cannot vanish: for any t choose n sufficiently
large that v(t/n)>0, and v(t)=v(t/n)^n. Thus log v(t) is continuous and additive
on nonnegative reals. It is -lambda*t, lambda>=0. The stated derivative at zero
identifies these lambda with the eigenvalues of L. Consequently V_t=exp(-tL).
This uses scalar Cauchy functional equations, rather than the source matrix ODE
argument. The proof covers degeneracy, a zero generator, and the zero-dimensional
space.

For the specified closure, use the canonical identification H* tensor H = End(H).
Its coevaluation corresponds to the identity; pairing after applying T is the
matrix pairing with that identity, sum_i T_ii. Spectral projectors P_lambda
therefore contribute rank(P_lambda)*exp(-t lambda). This verifies the canonical
closure value and dimensional block coefficients; the occurrence equality is
an explicit separate antecedent, not a derived physical action claim.

<a id="SPECTRAL-002"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-SPECTRAL-002 — finite counts and readouts

SU(2) spin j has dimension 2j+1, so the two-factor block has the product dimension.
The chosen symmetric Casimir is by definition 2(C_L+C_R)/R^2. On diagonal
j_L=j_R=k/2 it is k(k+2)/R^2, while the full package includes nondiagonal
modules; these are never treated as scalar functions on S3. The triangular
full-package count is sum_{a+b<=2m}(a+1)(b+1)=binomial(2m+4,4), using the
coefficient generating function (1-z)^(-5). The scalar count is
sum_{k=0}^m(k+1)^2=(m+1)(m+2)(2m+3)/6. At m=1 the full block data from exact
rational enumeration are dimension 15, eigenvalues times R^2 equal to 0, 3/2,
3/2, 4, 4, 3 with multiplicities 1,2,2,3,3,4; scalar dimension is 5.
The finite spectral traces in the source follow by the trace of each block.
The sole zero Casimir is (0,0), excluded in the zeta sum. Every retained
positive lambda contributes exp(-s log lambda), entire in complex s; finite
sums remain entire, including the empty m=0 positive spectrum (zero function).

For scalar parent counting put N=floor(sqrt(1+R^2 lambda)) for lambda>=0.
The exact count is sum_{n=1}^N n^2. Since N=R sqrt(lambda)+O(1), this is
R^3 lambda^(3/2)/3+O(lambda). This independently checks the table's Weyl term.
Resolvent poles, strict positivity for logarithms, and zero-mode exclusions
are required exactly as stated in the source process table.

<a id="COUPLING-010"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-COUPLING-010 — fixed typed equivariant coupling

Amendment requested during integration: the typed-coupling record has its own
argument rather than relying on the finite-dimension/Casimir certificate.
For G=SU(2)_L times SU(2)_R, write an irreducible mode space as
U_(a,b)=V_a tensor V_b. For two fixed source types and one fixed target type,
the universal tensor-product property and the direct-product action give
Hom_G(U_(a,b) tensor U_(c,d), U_(e,f)) canonically isomorphic to
Hom_SU(2)(V_a tensor V_c,V_e) tensor
Hom_SU(2)(V_b tensor V_d,V_f).
Each SU(2) tensor product is multiplicity free: V_e occurs exactly when
|a-c|<=e<=a+c with a+c-e an integer, and similarly
|b-d|<=f<=b+d with b+d-f an integer. Otherwise the corresponding Hom space
is zero. Thus both factors impose selection rules independently. Once bases
and a specific pointwise bundle contraction are fixed, the coefficients of
that contraction projected to target modes are coordinates of these Hom
maps, hence left and right Clebsch–Gordan coefficients times the contraction's
reduced coefficient(s). For successive couplings, expressing the same map in
different parenthesized tensor decompositions is exactly recoupling. Bundle
multiplicity/embedding data and the chosen contraction supply any additional
reduced coefficients; the statement does not assert that they are fixed by
representation labels alone. With the target or contraction unspecified,
there is no particular Hom map and hence no universal coupling coefficient.
This basis-free direct-product Hom argument checks the existing source
remark's limited, explicitly typed assertion, not a new physical coupling law.

<a id="POISSON-003"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-POISSON-003 — parent heat asymptotics

Put u=t/R^2. The shifted spectrum gives
Z(t)=exp(u)*sum_{n>=1} n^2 exp(-u n^2).
Poisson summation of a Gaussian gives
Theta(u)=sum_{n in Z}exp(-u n^2)=sqrt(pi/u)*sum_{ell in Z}exp(-pi^2 ell^2/u).
Differentiation is justified by absolute uniform convergence on compact
positive u intervals. Then
Z(t)=exp(u)*sqrt(pi)/(4u^(3/2))*
[1+2 sum_{ell>=1}(1-2*pi^2 ell^2/u)exp(-pi^2 ell^2/u)].
The bracket differs from 1 by an exponentially small quantity as u decreases
to zero. Expanding exp(u) gives exactly 1+u+u^2/2+O(u^3). The leading factor
sqrt(pi)R^3/4 equals Vol(S3(R))/(4*pi)^(3/2). This is an independent
spectral/theta-function certificate, not the source curvature invariant
substitution. It applies to the positive radius, positive small-time parent;
no finite fixed carrier has this singular short-time expansion.

<a id="ZETA-004"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-ZETA-004 — direct Dirichlet continuation

For Re(s)>3/2 the shifted source series is absolutely convergent. Binomial
expansion and absolutely convergent rearrangement give
zeta_Delta(s)=R^(2s)*sum_{j>=0}(s)_j/j! *[zeta_R(2s+2j-2)-1].
Here (s)_j is the rising factorial and zeta_R the Riemann zeta function.
On a compact s set, the large-j bracket decays exponentially (bounded by a
constant times 4^(-j)), and (s)_j/j! grows at most polynomially. Hence this
sum converges normally away from its isolated poles and supplies the
continuation to every compact subset of C. For j>=0, the only corresponding
pole is s_j=3/2-j, with residue
R^(3-2j)*(s_j)_j/(2*j!). All these half-integer residues are nonzero for
this round spectrum. The leading residue is R^3/2, equal to
Vol/(4*pi)^(3/2)/Gamma(3/2). Thus the source's possible-poles theorem holds
(and its displayed S3 pole list is correct). This route is independent of
source heat-Mellin continuation. The accompanying script checks the first
seven residues exactly against heat coefficients; the normal-convergence
argument proves the all-j statement.

<a id="COMPRESSION-005"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-COMPRESSION-005 — fixed bands and readouts

Let i_K and i_m be isometric inclusions of B_K and H_m into the parent
Hilbert space. Nestedness gives i_m J=i_K. Therefore
J* i_m* O i_m J = i_K* O i_K for every operator whose stated domain contains
H_m. This identity is exact for arbitrary O, with all maps defined on the
finite input band. For a spectral F(Delta), each E_k is invariant and the
restriction is diagonal, so the compressed operator is also the genuine
restricted operator and every F value is unchanged. This distinguishes
generic double compression from an invariant restriction.

Applying the same finite scalar functional to equal operators gives equal
values. For a trace this is trace equality; for fixed boundary data it is the
same matrix coefficient. Neither statement compares a trace on all H_m to a
trace on B_K, nor generates a performed readout. This separately checks the
source's process-readout corollary.

Given upstream m_p=1, the admissible scalar momentum bands are K<=1. No
large-m_p argument is involved. On a position frontier F containing B_K,
its orthogonal projection acts identically on that band. Complete-band
frontiers F=P_x(m_x) satisfy B_K subset F iff m_x>=K because all harmonic
shells are nonzero and mutually orthogonal. Physical frontier occurrence,
continued stage occurrence and momentum persistence remain the exact
upstream conditional/established inputs respectively.

<a id="WORD-006"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-WORD-006 — guard bands

Restricted ambient polynomials of total degree <=r span P_x(r). Their
product filtration is immediate from total degree, without invoking a
finite compressed multiplication identity. The intermediate vector after
j symbols has degree <=K+sum_{a<=j}s_a. Under m>=K+sum_all s_a each
intermediate projection is the identity. Induction proves equality of the
entire word to parent multiplication as vectors, hence zero norm remainder
on the declared input band. This holds for zero degree symbols, empty words,
and exact guard equality. It does not imply equality without that buffer.
The conditional stage rule F_0=P_x(1), F_{n+1}=span(F_n,E_1 F_n) gives
F_n=P_x(n+1) by polynomial degree decomposition, so substitution yields the
stated n+1 guard certificate. This verifies the existing stagewise import
within its admitted-rule antecedent and does not assert the rule occurs.

<a id="KERNEL-007"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-KERNEL-007 — Berezin symbol error

Use the orthonormal Chebyshev basis U_j for the S3 zonal semicircle measure
(2/pi)*sqrt(1-s^2) ds. For C_m(s)=sum_{j=0}^m (j+1)U_j(s), Parseval gives
integral C_m^2=d_m. The three-term recurrence
s U_j=(U_{j+1}+U_{j-1})/2, U_-1=0,
gives integral s C_m^2=sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(j+1)(j+2).
Thus the normalized kernel has integral s equal to 2m/(2m+3). Chord squared
on the unit sphere is 2(1-s), yielding exactly 6/(2m+3). This differs from
the source tensor-product/character coefficient derivation.

Positivity and Jensen/Cauchy-Schwarz give
|B_m f(q)-f(q)|<=L_f*E[physical chord]<=L_f*R*sqrt(6/(2m+3)).
Solving the squared inequality and taking the least nonnegative integer gives
exactly the printed ceiling bound. This includes m=0 and L_f=0. Tensoring
with a fixed identity is isometric in operator norm, so position-only tests
acquire no momentum error term; a genuinely two-factor symbol has a separate
fixed momentum concentration term, not an unproved vanishing limit.

<a id="BOUNDARY-008"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-BOUNDARY-008 — cutoff topology and operator identities

The source's scalar boundary claims can also be checked by a moment/kernel
route. The radius defect D=I-sum C_a^2 is supported only on E_m: multiplication
can leave the band only from that shell, and D=sum P M_a(1-P)M_a P.
SO(4) equivariance makes D a scalar on irreducible E_m. Independently,
Tr(sum C_a^2)=integral integral (x dot y)|C_m(x dot y)|^2 dσ(x)dσ(y)
=d_m*2m/(2m+3), by the recurrence calculation above. Hence
Tr(D)=3d_m/(2m+3)=(m+1)(m+2)/2. Divide by dim(E_m)=(m+1)^2 to obtain
D=(m+2)/(2(m+1))*Q_m, including m=0.

For the commutator, its support is also E_m. The O(4)-equivariant map from
bivectors into End(E_m) is a scalar multiple of rotation L_ab: SO(4) has one
copy each of the two adjoint types here and orientation reversal equates
coefficients. Take h=(x_a+i x_b)^m, m>=1. The complex raising coordinate
z=x_a+i x_b sends h entirely to E_{m+1}, so C_z h=0. The projection of
bar(z)h to E_{m-1} is alpha*z^(m-1). Since |z|^2 has the uniform [0,1]
law on S3, its beta moments give alpha=(1/(m+1))/(1/m)=m/(m+1).
Then ||C_bar(z)h||^2/||h||^2=m/(m+1). From
[C_bar(z),C_z]=2i[C_a,C_b] and L_ab h=i*m*h, the common coefficient is
1/(2(m+1)). At m=0 both sides vanish. Thus the printed commutator has the
correct coefficient and sign. Rotation weights range from -m to m, attaining
m on h, giving norm m/(2(m+1)). Radius norm tends to 1/2, as does the
commutator norm. Since Q_m annihilates every fixed finite band eventually
and both families are uniformly bounded, the defects converge strongly to
zero. The normalized radius trace is exactly 3/(2m+3).

The script independently builds coordinate compression matrices from an
ambient polynomial quotient and exact S3 moments at m=0,1,2,3. It verifies
all six commutators and radius formulas, supplying checkable controls
independent of a harmonic raising/lowering implementation.

For general well-defined compositions insert I=P+Q into PABP:
PABP=PAPBP+PAQBP. This proves the product defect. When D commutes with P,
[PDP,PM_fP]=P[D,M_f]P=P M_{Df}P, by the Leibniz rule. The finite smooth
band supplies the operator-domain core. These formulas do not make a
whole-carrier norm convergence claim.

<a id="FLAT-009"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-E3-FLAT-009 — extrinsic exponential chart

Embed S3(R) in R4 and take p=(0,0,0,R). The exponential is
exp_p(v)=(R sin(r/R) v/r, R cos(r/R)), r=|v|.
Differentiate directly. A unit radial variation has derivative of Euclidean
norm one. A tangential variation perpendicular to v has derivative multiplied
by R sin(r/R)/r. Cross terms vanish. The pullback metric therefore has radial
eigenvalue 1 and two tangential eigenvalues sinc(r/R)^2, without using the
source polar-coordinate metric formula.

On 0<rho<pi, d(sin rho/rho)/d rho has numerator
rho cos rho-sin rho. Its derivative is -rho sin rho<0 and it starts at zero.
Thus sinc^2 decreases strictly to zero and the displayed L-dependent lower
bound is sharp as a supremum approached as r increases to L on the open ball.
For 0<=rho<=1, sin rho/rho>=1-rho^2/6>=0 implies
1-sinc(rho)^2<=rho^2/3-rho^4/36<=rho^2/3.
No C^1, operator or dynamics estimate is implied. The flatness predicate is
therefore an explicit ratio check on the exact round branch, with no new
independent geometry assumption.

# Independent verification — Paper II-D batch 2

Reviewer: `/root/independent_checks`. Target: current v2.366 corpus,
`Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex`, lines 1017–2060.
The provisional assessment was recorded before receiving other reviewers'
findings. No batch2 replay, mapper or adversarial proposal was read.
A subsequent coordinator message identified the literal isotropy-group phrase
at line 1357; certificate TYPE-011 checks that phrase independently below.
All other certificates use exact source claims, definitions and narrowed
current-source imports. No paper was modified and no new framework theorem
or repair was developed.

<a id="CHIRAL-001"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-CHIRAL-001

Identify so(4) with bivectors in oriented Euclidean four-space. The Hodge
star has square one on bivectors and its positive and negative eigenspaces
have dimension three each. The Hodge star commutes with the orientation-preserving SO4 adjoint action;
differentiation gives [X,*Y]=*[X,Y], so its two eigenspaces are ideals. A
cross-ideal bracket belongs to both eigenspaces and therefore vanishes. The
induced metric is negative definite on compact rotation generators. Thus the two ideals are the compact real
su(2) factors. Writing spatial rotations and transvections in their
self-dual/anti-self-dual combinations gives exactly
L+ = (J+RP)/(2 hbar), L-=(J-RP)/(2 hbar).
This identifies the source's linear combinations by geometric self-duality,
rather than deriving the direct sum solely by its printed bracket expansion.
The inverse relations follow from adding/subtracting the two self-dual
projections. The construction needs R>0 and nonzero normalization hbar,
which are the declared kinematic normalization domains. It splits Killing
symmetry algebra, not the underlying single S3 carrier into two parents.

<a id="CENTER-002"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-CENTER-002

Realize spin j as Sym^(2j)(C2). The central -I acts as (-1)^(2j); hence the
diagonal Spin(4) center acts on type (jL,jR) by (-1)^(2(jL+jR)). This
constructively proves the descent criterion: a representation factors through
the quotient exactly when that kernel is trivial on it. The protected
(1/2,0) and (0,1/2) sectors therefore fail SO4 descent, while the coordinate
(1/2,1/2) type descends. This is a representation lift of one geometric
parent, not a new geometric parent.

At level one the central character is +1 on dimensions 1,4,3,3 and -1 on
dimensions 2,2. Thus H+ has dimension11, H- dimension4 and Tr Gamma=7.
Since Gamma is a represented involutive unitary, Gamma*=Gamma=Gamma^-1,
and its spectral projectors are (1±Gamma)/2. The adjoint action of Gamma on
End(H) has character (Tr Gamma)^2=49 and total dimension225, so its ±
eigenspace dimensions are (225±49)/2=137,88. This character computation
independently checks the source rectangular-block count; the eigenspaces
are the respective same-character and opposite-character Hom summands.

An equivariant vector map X:V_coord tensor H -> H must intertwine the
center. Since zc acts trivially on V_coord, its input/output H characters
agree, so X is central even. Rotation/transvection generators commute with
all central group elements, as do equivariant projectors. The commutant of
Gamma is a unital star algebra and is closed under finite functional
calculus, proving the inclusion for every word actually licensed by this
kinematic grammar. It does not assert all ambient End(H) operations are
physically generated. For an invariant central-odd bridge, Hom_G(H-,H+)=0
and Hom_G(H+,H-)=0: the irreducible sector supports are disjoint. Hence its
odd component must vanish by complete reducibility. This is an alternative
intertwiner-support proof of the existing no-bridge lemma.

On one irreducible sector, central conjugation is trivial even for a
spinorial representation. On a direct sum it is trivial precisely on
same-character blocks; opposite-character maps are not claimed to descend.
This certifies the operator-level descent scope in the source remark.

<a id="ANTIPODAL-HOPF-003"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-ANTIPODAL-HOPF-003

For g in SU2, quaternion multiplication gives
(-I,I):g -> -g, (I,-I):g -> -g and (-I,-I):g -> g.
The kernel of the Spin4 action consists exactly of (I,I),(-I,-I): if
agb^-1=g for all g, then a=b and a commutes with every SU2 matrix, hence
a=b=±I. Thus the antipodal isometry has exactly these two specified lifts,
which differ by the diagonal kernel. On scalar degree-k harmonic
polynomials antipodal parity is (-1)^k, while zc is +1 on every scalar
harmonic. On the scalar coordinate k=1 sector they already differ, so they
cannot be conflated with the 11+4 central grading.

Independently multiply the two-by-two Pauli matrices in
g=y4 I+i yj sigma_j and h=I+i alpha sigma_i+O(alpha^2).
Using sigma_i sigma_j=delta_ij I+i epsilon_ijk sigma_k gives the left action
velocity B_i-R_i and right action velocity B_i+R_i, where
B_i=y4 partial_i-yi partial_4 and R_i=epsilon_ijk yj partial_k.
Since U(alpha)=exp(i alpha Q), Q=-i times that real velocity. With the
declared J/hbar=-iR and RP/hbar=-iB, this gives
Q_H,L=(RP-J)/hbar=-2 L- and Q_H,R=(RP+J)/hbar=2 L+.
The sign and the swapped geometric/algebraic left-right labels follow
explicitly. Replacing right h by h^-1 reverses the right generator.
The exact script checks all three Pauli axes with zero residuals. A general
oriented unit axis follows by real linear combination, so these are not
isolated-axis numerical controls.

Exchanging the two simple ideals cannot be an inner automorphism of the
connected product group: conjugation preserves each simple ideal. A spatial
orientation reversal realizes the exchange and preserves the round metric.
Any marked Hopf axis/action is transported with that exchange; no assertion
that it stays fixed is needed. This verifies the chirality-symmetry remark
within the stated bundle/metric and selected-structure boundary.

<a id="TAGS-004"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-TAGS-004

This is the narrow imported measurement interface only, not a re-audit of
II-C. Given reducing effects E_j commuting with P±, the original E_j is the
sum P+ E_j P+ + P- E_j P-. For any assigned scalar outcome f(x_j), summing
that identity weighted by f preserves the original symbol exactly. Summing
j first instead gives the marginal P±, so the tagged probability is the
state's central population. These are identities of reducing block matrices
for every admitted source state; neither is a state-preparation theorem.

For the covariant endpoint rules cited by II-D, trace on either central block
is constant along the transitive sphere orbit; normalization of its integral
makes it the block dimension. For normalized equal-weight finite rules this
gives Tr(Pg E_j)=11/N and Tr(Ps E_j)=4/N. Therefore rho_p=p Pg/11+
(1-p)Ps/4 has identical untagged probabilities 1/N for all p, while the
tagged probabilities are p/N,(1-p)/N. Thus the exact moment preservation and
population-separation statement actually imported by II-D holds, without a
tomography or occurrence inference. No later II-D grading result is needed
to generate the upstream II-C projectors; their sector sums already exist.

<a id="CASIMIR-SCALAR-005"></a>

## BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-CASIMIR-SCALAR-005

The invariant quadratic forms on su2 direct-sum su2 form a two-dimensional
space: invariance annihilates cross terms between distinct perfect ideals,
and each compact simple ideal has its one-dimensional invariant quadratic
form. Thus there are two independent quadratic Casimir owners. On spin j,
write S^2=S_z^2+S_z+S_- S_+ and apply it to a highest-weight vector. Its
eigenvalue is j(j+1), and centrality gives the same eigenvalue on the whole
irreducible. The two factors' quadratic values can be varied independently
by taking (j,0) and (0,j), verifying independence and absence of hbar^2 in
the dimensionless convention. Higher functions of these Casimirs are not
being excluded by the word 'two'; the source explicitly discusses the
quadratic center and multiplicity-space freedom.

For scalar order-two operators, use an explicit jet calculation at the
north pole rather than assuming the source invariant-symbol statement.
In normal tangent coordinates its 2-jet functional has symmetric leading
coefficient matrix A, first-order vector b and scalar coefficient c.

## BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-SCHUR-006

For a unitary finite G module, let M_lambda=Hom_G(V_lambda,H). The evaluation

<psi,nabla*nabla psi>=||nabla psi||^2>=0 on smooth eigenspinors. Thus every

bound, not an assertion that the lowest eigenvalue squared equals3/(2R^2).
For the general closed Riemannian spin manifold in the source remark,

D^2=nabla*nabla+(1/2)sum_(i,j)c_i c_j R^spin_ij, with
R^spin_ij=(1/4)sum_(a,b)R_ijab c_a c_b.

establishes D^2=nabla*nabla+Scal/4 pointwise for arbitrary dimension and

>=min_M(Scal)/4.
Thus the general source remark's bound is justified in its full domain;

not a no-zero conclusion. For the round sphere its square-root bound is
sqrt(3/2)/R, below3/(2R). These claims and the distinction from the exact
gap follow without any physical dispersion.

# Independent E3 review of the two Paper II-D corrections

Source: Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_133.tex in the supplied update working
corpus v2.367. Reviewer: /root/independent_checks. Scope is exactly the two
corrected source objects and their actual proof statements; no other new
source claim was audited or edited in this review.

## BH-IID-EV-UPDATE-E3-G002

The new proof explicitly keeps K=SU(2)_diag and states that its action on
the tangent module p factors through K/{±I}=SO(3). This is correct:
p is the anti-diagonal tangent module {(A,-A):A in su(2)}. A diagonal
(u,u) sends it to (Ad_u A,-Ad_u A). The adjoint kernel consists exactly
of u=±I, while conjugation by unit quaternions rotates all imaginary
quaternions. Thus the effective quotient is SO(3); K itself has not
been identified with that quotient.

To verify the theorem independently, write a scalar order-two jet at a
point as a symmetric coefficient matrix A, a first-order vector b and a
zeroth-order scalar c. Stabilizer rotations diag(1,-1,-1) and
diag(-1,1,-1) force the off-diagonal coefficients and b to vanish;
quarter-turns about coordinate axes force the three diagonal entries
equal. Conversely A=aI,b=0 is invariant under every rotation. Transitivity
therefore gives a multiple of the metric Laplacian plus a constant,
with no invariant first-order remainder. The scalar zero-mode convention
removes that constant. On scalar harmonic degree k the two chiral
Casimirs each have j(j+1), j=k/2, so 2(C_L+C_R)/R^2=k(k+2)/R^2,
checking the retained radius normalization. The corrected proof and
original scalar theorem are verified at their stated R>0 scope.

## BH-IID-EV-UPDATE-E3-G004

The revised statement and proof explicitly attach the displayed squared
pair to the two original retained k0 spinor sectors, and explicitly deny
that they must remain the lowest full smooth-spinor values for arbitrary
real m. This exactly matches the operator calculation. For every real m,
the spin perturbation (m/R)I is local, self-adjoint and Spin(4)-equivariant,
is zeroth order and commutes with every scalar multiplication operator.
It is bounded for fixed R>0 and preserves the self-adjoint Dirac domain.
Consequently the principal symbol and coordinate commutators are unchanged.

The original retained spinor eigenvalues are ±3/(2R), so on those same
sectors the shifted squares are (m±3/2)^2/R^2 for every real m. At
m=3/2 the original negative k0 sector is zero; at m=-3/2 the original
positive k0 sector is zero. Each sector has complex dimension two.
Hence the retained scalar zero space acquires an additional spinor
summand, while the canonical m0 retained square has only its scalar
zero line. This proves the main no-rigidity conclusion without requiring
any global eigenvalue ordering.

The previous full-parent ordering witness is now consistent with the
printed qualifier: R1,m5/2 gives retained squares16,1, while the full
negative k1 mode shifts from -5/2 to0. The updated statement allows
precisely this situation. It does not discard that higher mode, weaken
the main no-go, or assert a new physical vacuum/Hamiltonian owner.
Thus the corrected source-as-printed statement and proof are verified
for all real m, and the prior ordering objection no longer applies.

No verdict was inferred from an audit status flag or from a script that
merely reprints statuses. The evidence is the explicit tangent-action,
jet and spectral-shift calculations above. No source/canonical graph edit,
new mechanism or new theorem was produced by this review.
